main_text.p: Max. cognitionem ascedere, perpetuo in rebus inferioribus subsistetes. At nos ita versemur in Physicis, ut Deum naturæ summū authorem, & cōseruatorem verè agnoscamus, amplectamur, & ex animo adoremus: atque ita statuamus nunquā eos [illegible, ~5 letters]ram posse cognoscere, qui naturæ authorem ignorant. Mihi vero de edendis his nostris institutionibus Physicis, cogitanti occurristi, Nobilissimeꝰ & amplissimeꝰ vir, cui hos labores nostros, quantulicunqueꝰ illi sunt, offerrem dicaremque: quod pios omnes viros & honestos non solum colas & vehementer ames: sed etiam quod liberalium artium & disciplinarum bonarum studio maximè flagres. Quod profecto ijs satis perspicuum est, ad quos tui nominis splendor peruenit. Nec vero militiæ & armorum peritia, qua velut generosissimi maiores tui, præditus es,

page.notes: Running head is printed in spaced capitals and is taken as the running title. The first word "Max." carries a decorative initial and is uncertain. The mark over "cōseruatorem" is read as a macron and may be a different mark. The word after "eos" is partly obscured by a blot and is marked illegible. The curled marks after "Nobilissime", "amplissime", "quantulicunque" and "peritia" are read as the -us suspension, and "peritia" may carry only a comma. "subsistetes" and "ijs" are printed as they appear.
